s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological decline with motor and speech impairment
salient_findings: Episodes of spasms and tremors in the right hand and forearm
Extensive nonenhancing lesions in the bilateral cerebral hemispheres on MRI
key_facts: Woman in her mid-60s
Initial presentation with episodes of spasms and tremors in the right hand and forearm
Underwent carpal tunnel release surgery
Tremors recurred 7 months later
Referred to a neurologist
Developed progressive right-sided weakness over 3 months
Developed dysarthria, hand tremors, slurred speech, and gait instability
Brain MRI showed hyperintensities throughout the bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter, corpus callosum, basal ganglia, thalami, midbrain, upper pons, and middle cerebellar peduncles
No contrast enhancement on T1-weighted fluid-attenuated inversion recovery MRI
Brain biopsy showed CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ lymphoma cells
Cerebrospinal fluid presence of lymphoma cells
Bone marrow negative for lymphoma cells

shortlist.label: Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Brain biopsy showed CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ lymphoma cells and cerebrospinal fluid presence of lymphoma cells

shortlist.label: Gliomatosis Cerebri
shortlist.why_kept: Extensive nonenhancing lesions in the bilateral cerebral hemispheres on MRI

shortlist.label: Intravascular Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive neurological decline with motor and speech impairment, and presence of lymphoma cells in cerebrospinal fluid

shortlist.label: Lymphomatoid Granulomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation and imaging findings to Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma

shortlist.label: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperintensities throughout the bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter on MRI, although less likely given the absence of immunocompromised state

raw.rationale: The presence of lymphoma cells in the cerebrospinal fluid and brain biopsy, along with the imaging findings of extensive non-enhancing lesions in the bilateral cerebral hemispheres, strongly supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Gliomatosis Cerebri
rejected.why: Lack of contrast enhancement and presence of lymphoma cells are not typical for gliomatosis cerebri

rejected.label: Intravascular Lymphoma
rejected.why: The imaging findings and biopsy results do not suggest intravascular involvement

rejected.label: Lymphomatoid Granulomatosis
rejected.why: The biopsy results and clinical presentation do not match this diagnosis, which typically involves the lungs and has a distinct histological pattern

rejected.label: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy
rejected.why: The presence of lymphoma cells and the specific imaging findings do not support this diagnosis, which is typically associated with JC virus infection and has distinct histological features
